subskill: Coordinate of the most profitable whole-number plan
prompt:
A print shop makes posters and banners. The table shows the ink and paper each item uses.
Item | Ink (milliliters) | Paper (sheets)
Poster | 15 | 6
Banner | 18 | 16
The shop has 249 milliliters of ink and 140 sheets of paper, earns a profit of $14 on each poster and $18 on each banner, and makes only whole posters and banners. In the plan with the greatest total profit, how many posters does the shop make?
explanation: Let x be the number of posters and y the number of banners. The conditions are 15x + 18y ≤ 249 (that is, 5x + 6y ≤ 83) and 6x + 16y ≤ 140 (that is, 3x + 8y ≤ 70), and the profit is 14x + 18y, which is twice 7x + 9y, so it is enough to maximise 7x + 9y. The two boundary lines meet at x ≈ 11.09, y ≈ 4.59. Rounding gives 11 posters and 5 banners, which needs 255 milliliters of ink, too much; rounding down to 11 and 4 is allowed and earns $226, but it is not the best. Write the profit two ways: 7x + 9y = (3/2)(5x + 6y) - x/2 ≤ 124.5 - x/2, and 7x + 9y = (9/8)(3x + 8y) + (29/8)x ≤ 78.75 + 3.625x. A value of 7x + 9y of 119 or more would need x ≤ 11 from the first and x ≥ 12 from the second, which is impossible, so 7x + 9y is at most 118. A value of exactly 118 needs 11 ≤ x ≤ 13; x = 11 and x = 12 give no whole y (9y = 41 or 34), and x = 13 gives y = 3: 195 + 54 = 249 milliliters of ink, 78 + 48 = 126 sheets, and a profit of 182 + 54 = $236. So the best plan makes 13 posters (and 3 banners). Choice 11 comes from rounding the corner. Choice 0 reads the table's rows the wrong way round (a poster using 18 milliliters and 16 sheets, a banner 15 and 6), which leads to 0 posters and 16 banners. Choice 16 swaps the two profits ($18 per poster, $14 per banner), which leads to 16 posters and no banners.
solve: let best=-Infinity, ans=null; for(let x=0;x<=40;x++) for(let y=0;y<=40;y++) if(15*x+18*y<=249 && 6*x+16*y<=140){ const v=14*x+18*y; if(v>best){best=v; ans=x;} } return ans;

distractor_solve.0: let best=-Infinity, ans=null; for(let x=0;x<=40;x++) for(let y=0;y<=40;y++) if(18*x+15*y<=249 && 16*x+6*y<=140){ const v=14*x+18*y; if(v>best){best=v; ans=x;} } return ans;
distractor_solve.11: const d=15*16-18*6; const x=(249*16-18*140)/d; return Math.round(x);
distractor_solve.16: let best=-Infinity, ans=null; for(let x=0;x<=40;x++) for(let y=0;y<=40;y++) if(15*x+18*y<=249 && 6*x+16*y<=140){ const v=18*x+14*y; if(v>best){best=v; ans=x;} } return ans;

mechanism: two supply lines meet at a non-integer corner
bound the profit two ways and check the few candidates
report the coordinate of the best plan
quantity_asked: number of posters in the unique plan with the greatest total profit

setup.i: two supply limits (ink and paper) given in a table; maximise profit
setup.ii: the best whole-number plan uses all the ink exactly, two posters past the rounded corner, with fewer banners
setup.iii: number of the first item in the most profitable plan

plugback.why: Trying 0, 11, 13 in order: for each poster count the student can find the best banner count and its profit (0 posters: 8 banners, $144; 11 posters: 4 banners, $226; 13 posters: 3 banners, $236), but a larger profit at one option does not show it is the greatest over all plans, so confirming 13 still needs the bound or a full scan. The key is at natural try 3 in any case.

0.why: Reading the table's rows the wrong way round gives each item the other's ink and paper use; the stem does not show which way that moves the poster count.

11.why: Rounding the corner skips the lattice search; the stem does not show whether the best plan has more or fewer posters than the corner.

16.why: Swapping the profits makes posters the better item; nothing in the stem says how far the poster count then rises.

shape_check: The stem hands over: the poster count is a whole number with 15x <= 249, so from 0 to 16. All four options survive. No parity is forced.
interior_parity_check: The middle values are 11 and 13: both two-digit odd numbers of the same form; neither is cleaner.
arith_class_check: 11 and 13 are odd; 0 and 16 are even. Nothing in the stem implies parity, and the key is not alone in any class.
